sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F168].
Revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F5][F6][F7][D161][D200][D238].
The FY2022 increase came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, primarily from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized prices, and the three years to FY2025 show a 5.3% CAGR [F8][D274][D844].
The table's revenue is a later recast, not the figure first reported: FY2025 is $51.8 billion here against $58.9 billion in that year's 10-K [F10][X10][R1].
The U.S. supplied 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and contributed 5.7pp of the 4.9% growth [D382][D384][D342].
Crude oil was 66.3% of FY2025 revenue but added only 0.1pp, while natural gas added 4.4pp on 37.4% growth [D551][D553][D586][D585].
Sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion in FY2025 on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, inclusive of Marathon Oil, partly offset by lower crude prices [P28].
Net income fell 13.6% while revenue rose 4.9%, so there was no operating leverage in FY2025 [D343][D342].
Diluted EPS fell 18.7%, faster than net income, as the diluted share count rose 6.1% [D345][D356].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
Net margin fell 3.3pp in FY2025, after a 3.9pp drop in FY2024 [D351][D317].
DD&A rose $1.9 billion in FY2025 on the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes, lifting D&A to 19.5% of revenue [P22][D330].
Production and operating expenses rose $1.6 billion on Marathon Oil and $216 million of restructuring severance [P24].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9%, so net margin sits below the operating result [D332].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, well above the 1.52x of FY2022 [F59][F20][D333][D226].
The FY2025 decline from $20.1 billion came from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [P6][F58][F59].
Free cash flow margin peaked at 24.1% in FY2021 against a 12.2% window median, but the pack has no free cash flow after FY2022 [D185][D834].
Capex was 12.9% of revenue in FY2022 and 1.35x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [D222][D228].
Net cash was $7.1 billion, or 12.1% of revenue, in FY2025, in the 100th percentile of six energy peers against a -7.7% median [D337][D338][D850][D851].

FY2025 uses of cash were $12.6 billion of capex and investments, $5.0 billion of buybacks, $4.0 billion of dividends and $0.9 billion of debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, above the stated 30% framework [D339][F59][P31].
Return on average equity fell to 12.4%, below the 14.9% peer median [D341][D853].
The revenue basis break is the main flag: every year in the table is a recast below the first-reported figure, so growth and margins mix presentations [R1][F10][X10].
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized commodity prices, partly offset by higher sales volumes [F8][D274][P47].
The FY2017 SG&A line is first-reported at $561 million against a later $427 million, a low-severity recast [X42][R3].
Segment revenue members sum to 227% of FY2025 consolidated revenue, so they cannot be added [R4].
If net margin falls below the FY2025 level of 15.4% in the FY2026 10-K, the decline since the 30.6% FY2022 high would extend a fifth year [F30][F27].
If operating cash flow falls below the FY2025 $19.8 billion, the flat-to-down trend since FY2022's $28.3 billion would persist [F59][F56].
If buybacks plus dividends exceed the FY2025 $9.0 billion, capital return would move further above the 30% of operating cash flow framework [D339][P31].
